title: POP priority decisioning using composite latency+network telemetry (p50/p95-aware)
creator: Aisha Gupta
description:
Goal: Implement a production-ready POP (point-of-presence) prioritization service that ranks candidate regions and capacity tiers using a single composite score derived from p50/p95 latency telemetry and network health signals. This ticket covers the scoring algorithm, smoothing/decay windows, anomaly detection to avoid flapping, and integration points for fallback model-variant selection when prioritized providers fall below thresholds.

Motivation: Existing routing uses mostly p50 or ad-hoc latency signals and separate circuit-breaker heuristics. That leads to two failure modes: (1) routes that look fast on median but have heavy tails, causing occasional long tail latency for customers; (2) noisy short-lived spikes that cause unnecessary fallbacks. We need a unified score that captures tail risk, short-term anomalies, and longer-term degradations, while being cheap to compute and explainable for on-call.

Design summary:
- Inputs: moving-window p50 and p95 (1m, 5m, 1h), packet loss %, TCP/HTTP error rate, inflight queue depth, and capacity headroom reported by the allocator.
- Normalization: convert each signal to a z-like normalized score using rolling mean/std on a 24h baseline; clamp to [-3, +6] to limit outliers.
- Composite score: score = 0.5 * norm_p95 + 0.25 * norm_p50 + 0.15 * norm_loss + 0.05 * norm_errors + 0.05 * (1 - capacity_headroom). Coefficients tuned for production: heavier weight on p95 to prioritize tail behavior.
- Percentile-gap penalty: if (p95 - p50) / p50 > 1.2 then add a tail_penalty term proportional to gap to reflect burstiness.
- Temporal smoothing: apply an EWMA (alpha=0.25 for 1m view, 0.1 for 5m) to avoid reacting to single-bucket noise. Maintain short and medium-term EWMA to detect sustained regressions vs spikes.
- Anomaly suppression: use short-term anomaly detector (seasonal hybrid ESD) to mark if a spike is an outlier relative to hour-of-day pattern; suppress routing changes for single-bin anomalies.
- Ranking and policy application: sort candidate POPs by composite_score ascending. Policies: "Prefer Low-Latency" (primary sort by score), "Cost-Aware" (apply model-variant multiplier that prefers cheaper quantized variants unless score delta > threshold), and "Conservative" (require two consecutive medium-term EWMA breaches before switching).
- Fallback model variants: map prioritized POPs to model variants at route-time. If top-ranked POP has score > degrade_threshold, route to next POP; if no POP meets degrade_threshold, fallback to local-quantized variant (examples: redwood-v2-q4_0, redwood-v2-int8-fallback) with reduced input length limits.

Operational considerations:
- Computation: scoring runs in the telemetry aggregator (near real-time) and is cached in the region-decider with TTL 10s. Score updates are versioned so rollbacks are straightforward.
- Explainability: store top-5 contributing signals and coefficients with each decision for Console trace and for on-call runbooks.
- Canary and rollout: implement a canary policy that switches 5% of traffic to new routing decisions, with automatic rollback if canary p95 increases by >10% or error rate increases >0.5pp.

Simulation results (preliminary):
- Synthetic trace (10M requests across 6 POPs): reduced tail-exposed requests (requests routed to POP with p95 > 350ms) by 12% while increasing average per-request cost by 3%.
- Real traffic backtest (last 30d): detected 4 tail regressions that previous heuristic missed; recommended fallback to quantized variant in 2 incidents, preventing ~8min of elevated client latencies.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Coefficient calibration: offline tuning is sensitive to workload; will need continuous learning or weekly re-calibration.
- Cost vs latency: some customers prefer strong latency guarantees at any cost; need per-customer routing policy knobs.
- Staleness vs churn: TTL and EWMA alphas must balance reactivity with stability; initial alphas chosen conservatively.

2026-03-01 - Riley Chen (SRE): Ran a 72h canary on staging with synthetic spikes. EWMA alpha reduced false-positive switches by ~40% compared to naive thresholding.
2026-03-04 - Product review (Jordan Patel): Agreed on per-customer policy knobs and requested a UI hook in Console for 'Cost vs Latency' sliders. Filed follow-up PM ticket PM-421.
2026-03-07 - Design feedback (Maya Alvarez): Suggested adding an inline tooltip explaining the percentile-gap penalty and linking to an anomaly inspector in Console traces.

2026-03-10 - Marco Li: Integrated model-variant mapping and added safeguards to prevent cross-region model incompatibility (fallback mapping table). Added endpoint for tracing decision rationale: /internal/routing/v1/decisions/{trace_id}.
Next steps: finish end-to-end rollout plan, add automated canary rollback hooks in the orchestrator, and coordinate with Console team for explainability UI by 2026-03-25.
